summary: Topsham, Sagadahoc County, ME tower: built after a 1931 decision to give districts lookouts; 1932 panoramic map of the tower; FFLA lists it standing; no staffing or access record found.

facts.status_note: FFLA lists it as standing with no cab-gone mark; the Eastern US Lookouts page we read gives no current status, and a 'gone' entry in our records could not be traced to a page read

events.note: Annual report for the fall of 1931 says a lookout was erected on Mt. Ararat; it does not give the exact date or the tower's height
360-degree panoramic map centered on the Ararat Mt. tower in Topsham, made by the Maine Forestry Service

evidence.supports: 1931 decision to give districts without a lookout tower one
evidence.quote: In the Fall of 1931 it was decided to do away with the handicap of certain districts not having a lookout tower.

evidence.supports: a lookout was erected on Mt. Ararat
evidence.quote: A lookout was erected on Mt. Ararat in Sagadahoc County.

evidence.supports: report describes new forty-seven foot steel stations without naming Ararat's
evidence.quote: five new forty-seven foot steel lookout stations and one dismantled one were erected on peaks in the Organized Towns

evidence.supports: 1932 panoramic map centered on the tower in Topsham
evidence.quote: 360 degree panoramic map centered on the Ararat Mt. fire tower in the town of Topsham, ME, 1932

evidence.supports: map made by the Maine Forestry Service
evidence.quote: Maine Forestry Service, Maine Department of Agriculture, Conservation and Forestry

evidence.supports: FFLA lists the tower as standing, with no cab-gone asterisk

corrections.why: The county is Sagadahoc. Digital Maine gives Sagadahoc County; the FFLA and Eastern US Lookouts pages spell it Sagadhoc, which looks like a typo carried through.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: FFLA lists the tower as standing, with no cab-gone mark. The Eastern US Lookouts page we read has history only and gives no status, so the 'gone' value in our records could not be traced to any page we read. Recorded as standing with low confidence.

sources.title: Ararat Mt. 1932
sources.publisher: Maine Forestry Service, Digital Maine (Maine State Archives)

notes_for_editor: Thin: one annual-report quote and one 1932 map. The record's 'gone' status conflict is unexplained; please check where that value came from. The Eastern page for Ararat has no status line in the text we read. A geocache listing (GCHCJD) reportedly describes a 1933, 50-foot tower still standing in 1998, but fetch_text returned only its title, so nothing from it is used. The 1931 report's 'forty-seven foot' stations are not tied to Ararat, so no height is recorded. No access or staffing source found, and no photo added.
